intended_object: The transfer map τ: H_q(X; R) → H_q(Y; R) on singular homology for a covering map p : Y → X whose fibres are all finite. It is induced by the chain map that sends a singular simplex σ of X to the sum of all its lifts to Y (May, Concise Course §16). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the companion lemmas.
explanation:
The definition applies the degree-q homology functor to `singularChainComplexTransfer`, and the lemma `singularHomologyTransfer_eq_map` holds by `rfl`. That chain map is built from `SSet.chainComplexTransfer`, which is the alternating face map complex applied to an equifibered transfer between simplicial objects. In each degree n its component is `sigmaConstTransfer`. That map sends the summand of a simplex s in the coproduct ∐ R to the finite sum of the summands of the simplices t with p∘t = s. The lemma `summandι_singularChainComplexTransfer_f` states this.

This is exactly the classical transfer, σ ↦ Σ of the lifts of σ. Three facts make it well defined:
- each simplex has finitely many lifts, because fibres are finite and lifts are unique once the image of a vertex is chosen;
- the construction commutes with face maps, because p is a covering;
- it therefore gives a chain map, and homology turns it into the transfer.

The library proves the expected property: if every fibre has d points, then transfer followed by p_* is multiplication by d.

The generality is natural:
- p can be any covering map with finite fibres; no connectedness or constant degree is assumed.
- The coefficients R are an object of any preadditive category with coproducts and homology. This is the same generality as Mathlib's `singularHomologyFunctor`.

Mathlib has no covering-space transfer for singular homology, so there is no more general counterpart.
